"Countries warn against travel to Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks"
By John Power, Al Jazeera. Photo credit: Social Media via Reuters.

On MONDAY Australia and New Zealand became the latest to issue advisories against travel to the kingdom, after similar warnings from the US, Canada, the UK, South Korea and Japan.
- Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade: avoid King Khalid International Airport and "reconsider" travel to other Saudi airports.
- New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade: do not travel to the Saudi capital's main gateway or the provinces of NAJRAN, JAZAN and ASIR for any reason; avoid "non-essential" travel to Saudi Arabia as a whole.
- US embassy in Riyadh (Sunday): reconsider travel to the kingdom, citing threat of attacks by Iran and the Iranian-backed Houthis.
- Global Affairs Canada: advisory against non-essential travel to ANY part of Saudi Arabia.
- South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs: citizens in Saudi Arabia should LEAVE unless on essential business; anyone planning travel should CANCEL.
- UK FCDO: avoid travel to Jeddah and Dammam, and to all airports apart from Medina International Airport, except for essential reasons.

"Saudi Arabia reels from FIVE ATTACKS ON ITS AIRPORTS IN LESS THAN A WEEK."
One killed, 11 injured Sunday at King Khalid (GACA). Saturday's Houthi strike on the same airport killed 13 and injured more than 300 - "marking the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade."
"The Houthis claimed responsibility for all four strikes on Saudi airports before Sunday's attack, WHICH HAS YET TO BE CLAIMED BY ANY GROUP."
King Khalid international airport AND King Fahd international airport in DAMMAM remain CLOSED, causing significant disruption to aviation across the Middle East.
Disruption also at King Abdulaziz International Airport, JEDDAH: MORE THAN 150 FLIGHTS CANCELLED and 374 DELAYED on Sunday, per Flightradar24.
BRENDAN SOBIE, independent aviation analyst and consultant in Singapore, told Al Jazeera: "As has been the case with the Iran war and the impact from that crisis on the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain, the impact of this latest crisis really depends on how long it lasts, how long Riyadh airport remains closed, and how long and to what extent are the restrictions once it reopens."
